ai.text:
The European Commission has proposed a regulation to set the rules for the EU's support to farming under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) for 2028 to 2034. The European Parliament would decide on it through the ordinary legislative procedure, on an equal footing with the Council. The proposal would be part of a wider EU budget package and would bring the CAP's funding into a single National and Regional Partnership Fund, with the aim of making support more flexible and better able to respond to crises.

The CAP is described as central to the EU, but farming faces serious pressures: it is hard to attract young people, climate change and biodiversity loss are affecting the sector, and there are economic pressures, reliance on imports, and geopolitical uncertainty. The proposal builds on earlier reforms and on the CAP Strategic Plans for 2023-27, which are seen as an effective way to run the policy, and it looks for ways to simplify delivery and link up with other spending areas.

The proposal sets several goals. It would direct income support more precisely toward farmers who help secure food supplies, keep farms and sectors economically viable, and protect the environment, while still letting farmers earn income from other sources. It also aims to make farming a more attractive career, help new and young people enter the profession, and reward farmers who work with nature and move toward more sustainable methods. Further goals include strengthening resilience to crises and risks, speeding up innovation and the shift to digital tools, and improving working and living conditions in rural areas.

In practical terms, the proposal sets out the environmental, climate and social parts of the policy, including priority areas for the environment and climate. It lists all the CAP interventions, the rules for income support, and how support is targeted. It includes a "Young Farmers Starter Pack", a package of help for young farmers starting out. It also covers cooperation, the LEADER programme, knowledge sharing and innovation, and rules on how CAP data is governed.

On money, the wider budget proposal for 2028-2034 places the CAP within the National and Regional Partnership Fund. A large share of that fund is reserved for farm income support, with a guaranteed minimum of EUR 293.7 billion, to give recipients stable and predictable support.
